per_finding.notes: Host removal is mostly complete: runtime value and detection, installers, bridge and generators, host-bundles/cursor, cursor-skill-source, .cursor and .cursor-plugin, command stubs, cursor-sb-agents tooling, global toolstack, picker and smoke scripts, CI step, doctor checks, config keys, README, CLAUDE.md and site are gone or clean. Still left: the e2e-live harness Cursor host, the enterprise-e2e-live suite asserting deleted Cursor files, the RFL routing to deleted skills and scripts, and gaps in the legacy cleanup (see issues).

Checked all 20 moot ids (R6-02/12/13/25/31, R7-02/03/04/05/11/15/20/24/25/26/28, R8-10/20, R13-26, R10b-19) against R*.json locations. Every primary file is deleted. The surviving files they name (session-verify.sh, paths.sh, silver-update SKILL, install-recommended-tools-global.sh, phase-lock hooks, sb-doctor.sh, render-agent-bundle.py) hold no Cursor code. All confirmed moot.

skills/silver-multi-ai-task, skills/silver-deep-research-multi-ai and their codex/skill-source mirrors are byte-identical to the merge base 94800f8. They reference no deleted file. test-provision-cursor-agents passes under claude and codex, and the python unit suite runs inside the green scripts suite.
A one-sentence edit (the 'graphify cursor install on Cursor' clause was dropped). sha256 ef9a5584... matches hooks/core-rules.sha256, and the plugin mirror is identical.
hooks.json has 2 matchers, both 'MCP'; no CallMcpTool remains in hooks/ or scripts/. This matches the decision to drop only Cursor-only names.

issues.problem: The cleanup moves ~/.cursor/hooks/toolstack away but leaves the hooks.json entries that point into it for session-bootstrap.sh (a sessionStart entry added by the old global-toolstack patch-hooks.py:324) and shell-compression.sh (a legacy entry). After the run, Cursor runs a missing script on every session start and every Shell call.
issues.evidence: Temp HOME probe (REVF-HC-probe/home). Before: sessionStart has 'bash $C/hooks/toolstack/session-bootstrap.sh' and preToolUse has 'bash $C/hooks/toolstack/shell-compression.sh'. After the run, both entries are still in hooks.json while hooks/toolstack has been moved into .silver-bullet-legacy-backup/. graphify-gate.sh was stripped correctly. Base patch-hooks.py registers session-bootstrap.sh and lists toolstack/shell-compression.sh in LEGACY_ROUTING_HOOK_MARKERS.
issues.suggested_fix: Add session-bootstrap.sh and shell-compression.sh to TOOLSTACK_GATES; better, derive the list from every script the base global-toolstack dir shipped. Add a test asserting that no hooks.json entry is left pointing into a moved directory.

issues.problem: This is a regression against the uninstall path it replaces. The base post-release-uninstall.sh cursor branch removed ~/.cursor/plugins/cache/alo-labs-agent-plugins/silver-bullet, ~/.cursor/plugins/cache/alo-labs-cursor/silver-bullet (sha symlinks into the alo-labs cache, created by install-cursor.sh:328) and the SB state files under ~/.cursor/.silver-bullet/. The new script handles none of them. The alo-labs-cursor links become dangling once alo-labs/silver-bullet is moved away.
issues.evidence: Probe: after the run, plugins/cache/alo-labs-cursor/silver-bullet/deadbeef (now dangling), plugins/cache/alo-labs-agent-plugins/silver-bullet/abc and .cursor/.silver-bullet/state all remain. Base: git show 94800f8:scripts/lib/post-release-uninstall.sh lines 58-77.
issues.suggested_fix: Add the exact paths cache/alo-labs-agent-plugins/silver-bullet, cache/alo-labs-cursor/silver-bullet (move the symlinks themselves) and the SB-only ~/.cursor/.silver-bullet state dir, or at least the file names base removed. Add tests for each.

issues.problem: HC deleted silver-agent-cursor, scripts/agent-cursor-delegate.sh, install-cursor-sb-agents.sh and scripts/lib/cursor-sb-agents, but the review-fix ladder still routes to them: grok/composer models (and the gemini fallback) go to /sb:agent-cursor with invoke scripts/agent-cursor-delegate.sh, the resolver's d21_hint and the SKILL tell users to run the deleted install-cursor-sb-agents.sh, and the RFL state hook always resolves with --host cursor. The decision says HC must not leave the RFL broken, and G6 (the redesign) has no branch yet.
issues.evidence: SB_CURSOR_SB_AGENTS_SKIP_PROBE=1 python3 scripts/review-fix-ladder.py --host cursor --json -> agents_missing:true, d21_hint 'bash scripts/install-cursor-sb-agents.sh --fix' (file absent). AGENT_HOST_CATALOG['cursor'].invoke='scripts/agent-cursor-delegate.sh' (absent); skills/silver-agent-cursor is deleted.
issues.suggested_fix: Merge HC only together with or after G6. Otherwise, as a stopgap in HC, remap grok/composer/gemini fallbacks to an existing host, make the hook resolve the detected host and drop the dangling hints. Record the open dependency in the report.

issues.problem: The e2e harness still has a Cursor host: it exports SILVER_BULLET_RUNTIME=cursor, sources the deleted tests/live/agents/cursor/agent.sh and runs the deleted scripts/install-cursor.sh. The enterprise-e2e-live structural suite (opt-in, SB_ENTERPRISE_E2E_LIVE=1) now fails 6 assertions about the deleted Cursor adapter, hosts.json branches, runbook text and matrix timeouts, and it pins the leftover 'cursor/agent.sh' line in helpers.sh.
issues.evidence: bash tests/run-all-tests.sh tests/enterprise-e2e-live/test-enterprise-e2e-live-suite.sh -> 195 passed, 6 failed (e.g. 'cursor host adapter exists - missing scripts/enterprise-e2e/lib/adapters/cursor.sh').
issues.suggested_fix: Remove the cursor branches from tests/e2e-live/helpers.sh and the Cursor assertions from the enterprise suite. Re-run that suite.

issues.problem: The SB_FIVE_TOOL_LIVE block and its header comment run the deleted tests/live/test-live-five-tool-stack-cursor.sh and mention test-five-tool-prerelease-cursor.sh. The block is dead code.
issues.suggested_fix: Delete the block and the comment lines.

issues.problem: Smaller cleanup gaps. (a) A hooks.json entry whose program is codex-hook-adapter.sh without a bridge is not stripped, although the old merge treated it as SB's. (b) A 'user-agentmemory' MCP server that patch-mcp.py could write is not covered by MCP_NAMES. (c) An unrelated malformed mcp.json aborts the run with rc=1 after hooks.json has already been rewritten, so agents, rules, toolstack and plugins are skipped.

issues.suggested_fix: Handle each step's ConfigError separately (report it, continue, exit non-zero at the end). Add the codex-hook-adapter.sh program rule and the user-agentmemory name.

issues.suggested_fix: The orchestrator precedent (F2) is to accept merge commits as they are. Note it.

cleanup_script_verified_ok: Identifies entries by exact markers and names (generated agents need marker + frontmatter + name match; rules need an exact description line; toolstack needs the exact common.sh header and toolstack.json state_dir). User entries were kept: my-agent.md, an unmarked sb-fake.md, a symlinked agent, leanctx.mdc with a different description, a user mygate.sh in hooks/toolstack, an echo command mentioning silver-bullet, other@x in the registry, a user agentmemory MCP server via npx. A symlinked hooks.json stayed a symlink and its target got a .sb-backup. Moved items go to the backup bucket. A second run is a no-op, --dry-run changes nothing, and it never installs.
